# IP-03 Brief — Delivery, Capacity, Risk, and Verification Strategy

## Objective

Turn accepted scope and dependency reports into a capacity-safe delivery strategy, milestone plan, sprint detail for the first 30 percent of work, phase-level roadmap for the remainder, risk register, test strategy, deployment gates, and requirement traceability proposal.

## Inputs

- Accepted `IP-01-scope-report.md` and review.
- Accepted `IP-02-dependency-report.md` and review.
- `docs/.preflight-report.json`.
- `docs/design/visual-office-frontend-execution-plan.md`.

## Planning assumptions

- Two-week sprints.
- Three bounded delivery lanes: backend/data, frontend, and verification/security.
- Nominal capacity is 20 points per lane per sprint, but planned committed work must reserve at least 25 percent total contingency and must not exceed effective capacity.
- Risk and contract work is front-loaded; vertical slices are preferred.

## Output

Write only `docs/.rwang-tasks/CR12-FEAT34/IP-03-delivery-report.md`. Do not edit the final plan, source documents, ledger, graph, code, schema, generated artifacts, or Git state.

## Required content

- Team/lane responsibilities and RACI-style ownership.
- Sprint-by-sprint detail for the first 30 percent of implementation; later work at phase level.
- Capacity math, estimates, 25 percent or greater buffer, and no overloaded sprint.
- Milestones, entry/exit gates, acceptance evidence, release strategy, rollback strategy, observability, and handoff.
- Risk register with probability x impact and mitigations.
- Requirement-to-work-package-to-test traceability structure.

## Review hard gates

Completeness, traceability, consistency, capacity correctness, and evidence-backed readiness language must all pass.
